newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt mixed on extremely low volume.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mixed on extremely low volume.

text.p: Brady bonds were mixed in light activity on Monday but traders said buying opportunities were beginning to emerge given the sharp drop in the U.S. Treasury bond market on Friday.
"Given the fall-off in the credit markets, people are likely to start looking to get in at these levels," said an emerging market trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
But traders expected the Brady bond market to trade in a narrow range until next week, when a slew of key U.S. inflation reports are scheduled to be released.

Given the sharp rise in U.S. non-farm payrolls and a strong National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) report on Friday, traders said the market will focus on inflation data as a gauge of what the Federal Reserve's next move will be later this month.
The next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting will convene on August 19.
Among Eastern European credits, Russia continued to steal the spotlight amid hopes that a debt restructuring agreement with the London Club of commercial bank creditors would close in September.
"I think they would like to achieve that (the closing) by late September," said one trader, who noted the price movement had largely reflected a reduction in the deal risk.
Russian Vnesheconombank dollar-denominated loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were 1/4 firmer at 96-1/2 bid and its PRINs RUPRIN=RR were 1/4 higher at 70-1/2 bid.
Latin Brady bonds were unchanged to slightly lower.

Of the major Latins, Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 1/8 softer at 83-1/8 bid, Mexican pars MX625L19=RR were unchanged at 81-1/8 bid and Argentine Frbs ARFLC05=RR were 1/8 weaker at 95-1/8 bid. --Diane Craft, London Newsroon +44 171 542 5110
